sentences.text: This bird possessed an unusually long beak that reached 68% of the total skull length. It also had many small teeth, most of which were located on the bottom jaw.
The preserved skeleton includes feather remains and gastroliths, which are stones birds swallow to help grind food.
The species Changzuiornis ahgmi was named and described in 2016 by a team including Huang Jiandong and Julia A. Clarke. The holotype fossil was found in the Aptian-aged Jiufotang Formation.
Changzuiornis is classified within the Ornithurae and belongs to the family Gansuidae.
Changzuiornis was an extinct ornithuromorph bird that lived in present-day China during the Early Cretaceous. It lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
Researchers suggested that Changzuiornis might be the same genus as Juehuaornis, which would mean Juehuaornis has priority.
